name: Old Saxon

ancestors.notes: Ingvaeonic base; closely related to Old English

notes: Old Saxon (~800–1100 CE). Ancestor of Low German (Plattdeutsch). Major text: Heliand (~830 CE) — a Saxon gospel harmony in alliterative verse. NO HIGH GERMAN CONSONANT SHIFT: OS p, t, k unchanged (cf. OHG pf/ff, tz/ss, hh). OS makōn vs. OHG mahhōn 'to make'; OS water vs. OHG wazzer 'water'. Closely related to Old English and Old Frisian (all Ingvaeonic). Preserved þ as interdental, like OE. Source: Gallée (1993), Robinson (1992). `graphemes.v` was added because manuscript orthography interchanges b/ƀ/u/v/f for the single labiodental fricative phoneme that ⟨f⟩ also spells (Gallée 1910, pp. 126-128, 161, discusses this graphemic variation, e.g. `sivon` beside `sibun` 'seven'); the cached wikipron gold independently confirms it, transcribing every v-spelled word (avand, bokstaf's -av, geva, hovidmal, therva, etc.) with the same [f]/voiced-fricative alternation already modelled for ⟨f⟩, never with a distinct [v] phoneme. Two findings were checked but not acted on: unlike its Middle Low German descendant (gml), Old Saxon itself does not reduce unstressed-syllable vowels to schwa -- final -a in this gold overwhelmingly stays [ɑ] (19 of 21 -a-final words) rather than merging, consistent with Holthausen (1921) §147, so no `positional_graphemes`/`stress` block was added; and the gold's short ⟨a⟩ is transcribed [ɑ] in 186 of 191 tokens against only 5 as plain [a], which matches the back-vowel value modern surveys (e.g. the Old Saxon phonology summarized from Gallée 1910 and Lasch 1914) give for this phoneme, but Holthausen (1921) §40 only says short a is 'wie im Nhd.' (as in Standard German) without committing to a cardinal value, so this remains a measured distributional observation, not a sourced rule, and the grapheme table keeps [a]/[aː] pending a citation that states the quality explicitly.

sources.author: Gallée, J.H.
sources.title: Altsächsische Grammatik (2nd ed.)
sources.notes: Discusses the manuscript interchange of ƀ, b, u, v and f for a single labiodental fricative phoneme (e.g. sivon beside sibun 'seven'), used to source graphemes.v.

sources.author: Holthausen, F.
sources.title: Altsächsisches Elementarbuch (2nd ed.)
sources.notes: §40 gives short a, i, o, u the same value as in Standard German without specifying a cardinal vowel quality; §147 shows unstressed final -a is retained rather than reduced in Old Saxon, used to justify not copying gml's schwa-reduction rule onto osx.
